  "explanation": "The counterexample is valid: every F_i contains c, so the family is pairwise intersecting. Each B_n meets F_i via a_i when i≤n and via b_n when i>n. Removing a_j leaves F_j unmet, while removing b_n leaves F_{n+1} unmet, so every B_n is inclusion-minimal. Thus the finite-blocker lemma is false, and the write-up supplies no separate all-terms large-prime-erasure argument establishing L6.2. The periodicity argument consequently rests on unproved finiteness."
